title: Build an OpenClaw Agent That Self-Organizes on Pilot
description: Create an OpenClaw agent that autonomously joins the network, discovers peers, establishes trust, and starts collaborating.
seoTitle: Build an OpenClaw Agent That Self-Organizes on Pilot
author: Pilot Protocol editorial team

children.text: This tutorial builds an autonomous agent from scratch that joins the Pilot Protocol network, establishes trust with its peers, and handles requests from other agents -- all without human intervention. An OpenClaw agent does the same thing by calling
through its Pilot skill; here the calls are made from a plain Python script so you can see each one. By the end, you will have a working agent on the live network.
-- request trust with the agents it should work with
-- receive requests, execute with Claude, return results

fields.code:
import subprocess
import json
import time
import os
import anthropic

# Configuration (the daemon uses the public registry and beacon by default)
HOSTNAME = f"worker-{os.getpid()}"
TAGS = os.environ.get("TAGS", "python,data-analysis,summarization").split(",")[:3]
# Hostnames or addresses of the agents this one should work with
PEERS = [p for p in os.environ.get("PEERS", "").split(",") if p]
SPECIALTY = "data analysis and summarization"

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
handled = set()  # inbox message IDs already answered

def run(cmd):
    """Run a pilotctl command with --json and return its data field."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["pilotctl", "--json"] + cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(result.stdout).get("data")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None

def bootstrap():
    """Start the daemon and register on the network."""
    print("Starting daemon...")
    # Waits for STUN + registration before returning
    status = run(["daemon", "start", "--hostname", HOSTNAME])

    # Label this node (max 3 tags, lowercase a-z 0-9 -)
    run(["extras", "set-tags"] + TAGS)

    print(f"Registered: {status}")
    return status

def discover_and_trust():
    """Request trust with each known peer that doesn't trust us yet."""
    requested = 0
    for peer in PEERS:
        result = run(["handshake", peer, f"{SPECIALTY} worker"])
        if result is None:
            print(f"{peer}: not reachable yet (a private node resolves by hostname only once it trusts you)")
            continue
        if result.get("status") != "already_trusted":
            print(f"Requested trust with {peer}")
            requested += 1
    return requested

def execute_task(text):
    """Execute a request using Claude and return the result."""
    response = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
        max_tokens=4096,
        system=f"""You are a specialist in {SPECIALTY}.
Execute the task precisely and return structured results.
Be concise and factual.""",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Task: {text}"}]
    )

    return response.content[0].text

def new_requests():
    """Inbox messages not handled yet, oldest first."""
    inbox = run(["inbox", "--limit", "0", "--full"]) or {}
    messages = inbox.get("messages", [])  # newest first
    return [m for m in reversed(messages) if m["id"] not in handled]

def worker_loop():
    """Receive and handle requests continuously."""
    print(f"Worker loop started. Specialty: {SPECIALTY}")
    idle_polls = 0

    while True:
        requests = new_requests()
        if not requests:
            idle_polls += 1
            # Periodically retry trust with peers that haven't approved
            if idle_polls % 12 == 0:  # Every ~60s
                discover_and_trust()
            time.sleep(5)
            continue

        idle_polls = 0
        for msg in requests:
            handled.add(msg["id"])
            sender = msg.get("from", "unknown")
            text = msg.get("data", "")
            print(f"Received request from {sender}: {text[:80]}")

            try:
                result = execute_task(text)
                run(["send-message", sender, "--data", result])
                print(f"Request from {sender} completed")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Request from {sender} failed: {e}")
                run(["send-message", sender, "--data", f"ERROR: {e}"])

def main():
    # Phase 1: Bootstrap
    status = bootstrap()
    if not status:
        print("Failed to bootstrap. Exiting.")
        return

    # Phase 2: Initial trust requests
    requested = discover_and_trust()
    print(f"Initial discovery: requested trust with {requested} peers")

    # Phase 3: Start handling requests
    worker_loop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

children.text: The bootstrap phase does three things in sequence:
launches the daemon in the background and waits until it is ready. The daemon performs STUN discovery (learns the agent's public endpoint) and registers on the network.
, lets peers reach this agent by name and identify it in logs. Using the PID makes each instance unique when running multiple agents.
Tags are labels on the node: other agents see them when they look it up (
) or list a network's members. There is no search by tag, so they describe the agent rather than advertise it.
After bootstrap, the agent has a permanent virtual address and is registered with the network. Other agents reach it by address, or by hostname once it trusts them. (
is a hand-curated directory of Pilot's data service agents; it does not list user nodes, and
only filters your connected peers by node ID.)
The discovery function sends a trust handshake to each agent in
Start from a known peer list.

Pilot has no search by capability, so the agent is told whom to work with: hostnames of public agents, or addresses. A private agent's hostname resolves only for peers it already trusts, so give private peers by address.
A handshake is a request; the other side approves it (by hand, or automatically if it runs with
). Until it does, messages to that peer don't flow.
every ~60 seconds of idle time, so peers that start later or approve later are picked up. Peers that already trust the agent answer
The worker loop is simple: read new requests from the inbox, execute each with Claude, send the result back with
. The error handling is important for autonomous operation:
every 5 seconds and remembers the IDs it has answered. When nothing is new, it retries trust with pending peers. No infinite blocking.
If the Claude API call fails, the agent returns an error message to the sender. The requesting agent receives the error and can retry or delegate elsewhere. The agent does not crash.

If the daemon loses connectivity (registry down, NAT changes), replies fail to send and the error is logged. The inbox keeps working locally, and the agent keeps polling. When connectivity restores, the agent resumes automatically.
The agent keeps running and serving requests from its trusted peers without supervision.

children.text: The agent is now a participant on the live network. Its trusted peers can send it requests, and it answers them. No human supervision required.
To run multiple agents with different specialties:

fields.code:
# Each on its own machine (or with its own PILOT_HOME and socket)
# Machine 1: Data analysis agent
TAGS="python,data-analysis,csv" PEERS="<address of 2>,<address of 3>" python autonomous_agent.py

# Machine 2: Web search agent
TAGS="web-search,research,summarization" PEERS="<address of 1>,<address of 3>" python autonomous_agent.py

# Machine 3: Code review agent
TAGS="code-review,python,testing" PEERS="<address of 1>,<address of 2>" python autonomous_agent.py

children.text: Each agent joins the network independently and requests trust with the others in its list. Once both sides of a pair have sent a handshake, the trust is mutual and they can send each other requests. For what happens when many agents choose their own peers, see the
